$comment: Authoritative crosswalk from OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 codes to the 2026 edition. The 2026 revision is a RENUMBERING plus one rename/re-scope: no entry was added and none removed, so the mapping is a bijection over LLM01-LLM10. This file is the single source of truth for the migration; scripts/migrate_owasp_llm_2026.py reads it rather than hardcoding the permutation.

LLM01.scope_change: Expanded to cover cross-modal attacks that hide instructions in image or audio content, plus tool output, intermediate reasoning, and persistent memory as delivery surfaces.

LLM02.scope_change: Explicitly enumerates reasoning traces, tool-call arguments, embeddings, and observable inference properties as disclosure surfaces.

LLM03.scope_change: Now accounts for the trust failure when a promoted model artifact is not what it claims to be; model provenance and conversion/merge workflows are first-class attack surfaces.

LLM05.scope_change: Now spans insecure code that assistants generate at scale. Largest single drop in the 2026 edition.

LLM06.scope_change: Largest promotion in the 2026 edition; the project leads call it the most consequential move on the list.

LLM07.scope_change: Renamed and re-scoped from the system prompt specifically to ALL non-user-facing content assembled into the model's context: developer instructions, retrieved policy text, tool and function schemas.

LLM08.scope_change: Extended beyond RAG to vector-backed agent memory, semantic caches, and deduplication pipelines.

LLM09.scope_change: Reframed as a system-level failure: incorrect output consumed by downstream components and agents, not only by humans.

LLM10.scope_change: Emphasis on cost asymmetry, extended-thinking/reasoning output budgets, and MCP-style tool amplification.

migration_scope.applied: Code renumbering only. Each entry's owasp_llm array is rewritten through the bijection above, preserving the risk concept assigned to that entry.
migration_scope.not_applied: No re-classification. Several 2026 entries widened their scope (see scope_change above); incidents that would newly qualify under a widened entry were NOT added, because that requires re-running classifiers over incident descriptions. Re-classification is deliberately out of scope for this migration - see docs/audits/WS0-T3-cascade-2026-07-18.md for why description-coupled reclassification is treated as a hazard here. Adding those mappings is annotation work, not a migration.
